kai-ml: Uploaded harmonium-7b-v2 quant experiments and the eval CSV. Quick legal check: the upstream license snippet looks like 'Non-Commercial; attribution required; no redistribution of model weights'. Can we (a) serve quantized weights to Dedicated customers, (b) include quantized weights for Private deployments, or (c) keep hosted inference only? Also seeing quality delta after 4-bit quant: embedding cos-sim avg drop ~0.03 and Rerank MRR down 2.1%. Thoughts?
ryan-quant: short summary: 4-bit q4_0 -> latency -28%, GPU mem -2.1x, generation P95 improved. But embed cos sim -0.03, MRR -2.1%. Quick paste of numbers: ```baseline float16: emb_cos 0.912, mrr 0.287
q4_0: emb_cos 0.883, mrr 0.281
q8_0: emb_cos 0.900, mrr 0.285```
kai-ml: tagging @rita-legal — is the phrase 'no redistribution of model weights' explicit enough to block delivering quantized binaries? If hosting-only is allowed, can we still ship an inference-optimized artifact (a container with runtime + original weights fetched at deploy time)?
rita-legal: quick read: 'no redistribution of model weights' typically means we cannot provide weight binaries to third parties. Hosting inference as a service is often allowed under NC terms, but depends on whether license treats 'providing a hosted service' as a form of use. If attribution required, we must include the attribution in customer-facing docs. For Dedicated/Private: shipping the actual quantized binary to a customer likely violates redistribution clause unless we get a separate license.
eval-bot: perf-summary: latency -28%, mem -2.1x, emb_cos delta -0.029, rerank_mrr delta -0.006 (q4_0) :warning:
deployer-bot: note: we currently build per-customer containers that bake in weights when targetting Private installs (air-gapped). That flow would copy weights into customer artifact.
ryan-quant: possible technical mitigation: serve quantized runtime + pull original weights at runtime from an upstream controlled endpoint and quantize in-node (on first startup) so we never store a redistributed binary. But for air-gapped/private installs that won't work.
kai-ml: practical ask: can legal add a catalog flag like REDISTRIBUTION_DISALLOWED and REQUIRES_ATTRIBUTION so we can gate Dedicated/private onboarding? Also want to surface perf regressions in eval dashboard for product to decide whether quality delta is acceptable.
rita-legal: yes I can add a red flag to model catalog and file a partner-legal ticket to request a redistribution exception for Dedicated/Private customers. Short term: mark harmonium-7b-v2 as 'HOSTING_OK_REDIS_NO' and 'ATTRIBUTION_REQUIRED'. For sales: we must not ship weight files; for Dedicated we can run a hosted variant under contract until license updated. I'll draft a customer-facing attribution blurb.
kai-ml: thanks. Ryan — can you add a short note to the eval ticket enumerating which benchmarks break (ranking/embeddings) so PD can review? I'll also add a console flag to block bake-in weight builds for models with REDISTRIBUTION_DISALLOWED.
ryan-quant: on it — will attach eval slices and a short repro script: ```python
# repro cos sim drop
from datasets import load_dataset
# run embedding diff script...
```
rita-legal: one more: if a customer requests Private deployment and signs a commercial license, we can potentially ship quantized binaries under a negotiated SPLA. I'll coordinate with biz-ops.
kai-ml: perfect. tagging next steps: (1) legal flag + ticket, (2) eng add bake-in guard, (3) attach eval slices and repro, (4) product decide acceptable MRR tradeoff. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
